title: GRIT as a guarantee of success for young elite athletes and young elite musicians
summary:
Background:
The GRIT scale (“grit” means “grit” in English: “guts, courage, doggedness”) comes from positive psychology and attempts to measure a person’s “grit” to achieve a long-term goal regardless of how difficult it is or what obstacles have to be overcome. The scale originated in the USA, where Angela Duckworth, a professor at the prestigious University of Pennsylvania, studied the admission criteria and prospects of success of young cadets at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, which is considered elite and outstanding. Here she was able to show that a high score on the GRIT scale was a reliable parameter for predicting who would successfully complete the strict admission requirements and exams and graduate from the academy. The GRIT scale measured two personality facets: maintaining a constant interest in something and maintaining a high level of performance despite all resistance or persistence.(1) The inclusion criteria did not include any other competence or skill or characteristic that had comparable predictive power, which allows the conclusion that perseverance or "GRIT" is a decisive parameter. Previous research results show that "GRIT" can also be used to anticipate professional and academic success (2) and thus the GRIT model can also be applied to other areas.
As described above, Angela Duckworth was able to show that the GRIT value is a reliable parameter for determining whether someone is able to pursue a long-term goal to the end. In the case of the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, a high GRIT value correlated with a 62% higher chance of overcoming the first major hurdle, the summer training camp called the "Beast" (OR = 1.62; p < 0.001) (1).
Previous publications on GRIT show that the scale can easily be transferred to other areas, as long as the target is a long-term goal or challenge.

In the field of professional sport, the work of Larkin et al. (2015) from the University of Sydney is particularly worth mentioning. Studies with young soccer players
(U13-U15) who took part in the Australian national youth football championship showed that high GRIT values ​​correlated with high sport-specific commitment, good performance in perceptual-cognitive skill tests and the ability to make quick decisions. (6)
In addition, there are still no GRIT studies examining young top athletes and especially young top musicians. This study is therefore intended to examine possible promising personality traits as part of a GRIT cross-sectional study as part of a doctoral thesis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
young top athletes (including FC Bayern Munich basketball, Adler Mannheim ice hockey) and young top musicians (Munich University of Music and Theater, possibly from other music universities and/or orchestras such as the Young German Philharmonic ...)
signed consent to participate in the study, in the case of minors, an additional signed consent from the parents for their child to participate in the study
Completion of the entire questionnaire
Exclusion criteria:
inclusion criteria not met or subsequently withdrawn consent to use the collected data for study evaluation
